# Source Map — INEGI ENOE 2022Q4 Technical Note (GOV-017, AMLO 2022, Ch.5B)

## Document frame
- **Type/role:** INEGI quarterly technical note for ENOEN, Q4 2022. Official statistical body; results-bearing with methodological annex. (p.1, p.21–p.22)
- **Coverage:** Population 15+; national, 32 entidades federativas, 39 metropolitan areas (cities/areas metropolitanas with más de 100 mil habitantes), four locality-size strata. Probabilistic, two-stage, stratified, clustered design; five rotating panels. (p.21–p.22)
- **Comparability flags:** From Q3 2022 onward, **fieldwork returned to face-to-face only** (mixed phone+face-to-face during the Q3 2020–Q2 2022 ENOEN period). Pandemic-era PNEA-disponible classification (incl. ausentes temporales con vínculo and persons with necesidad o deseos de trabajar) operated Q3 2020 → Q2 2022; **discontinued** from Q3 2022 — pre-pandemic criteria retomaron. Microdata back-rebuilt to Q1 2014 using new population estimate. ENOEN program concludes with Q4 2022; ENOE monthly+quarterly resumes with January 2023 reference month. (p.21, p.22–p.23; footnote * p.3)
- **Seasonal adjustment:** X-13ARIMA-SEATS; adjusted and original series both reported. (p.23)

## Atomic claims (with locators; observed vs interpretive)

- **Observed (national, Q4 2022):** PEA 60.145 M; participation 60.4 % (vs 59.7 % Q4 2021, +0.8 pp). Occupied 58.349 M (97.0 % PEA, +0.7 pp); Unemployed 1.796 M (3.0 % PEA); long-term (>1 yr) unemployment 2.0 % (−2.2 pp). PNEA 39.370 M (39.6 %; −352 k). Informal workers 32.157 M (TIL1 55.1 %, −0.7 pp). Suboccupation 4.4 M (7.5 %, −3.1 pp). TCCO 30.4 % of occupied (salario mínimo equivalente base enero 2022). (p.2; p.3 Cuadro 1; p.10; p.11 Cuadro 5; p.14 Cuadro 7; p.15–p.16 Cuadro 8 / Gráfica 6)
- **Observed (sex distribution, Q4 2022):** PEA men 35.746 M (76.5 %); women 24.400 M (46.2 %; +1.6 pp y/y). Women in informal sector +736 k y/y; men −188 k. (p.2; p.11 Cuadro 5)
- **Observed (sector, Q4 2022):** Tertiary 62.7 %; Secondary 24.9 %; Primary 11.8 %. Comercio +279 k; manufacturing +260 k; servicios diversos +201 k; restaurantes/alojamiento +217 k. (p.6; p.8 Cuadro 3)
- **Observed (subordinate wage workers, Q4 2022):** 39.775 M (68.2 %). Health-care access 22.651 M (56.9 %; +1.1 M y/y). Written contract 22.863 M; without contract 16.302 M (16.301 660). ≤1 minimum wage 11.094 M; >1 to ≤2 minimum wage 16.003 M (16.002 653). (p.9 Cuadro 4)
- **Observed (locality-size, Q4 2022):** Urban-high (≥100 mil hab. o capitales de estado) hosts 49.5 % of occupied; rural (<2,500 hab.) 20.4 %; urban-low (2,500–14,999) 14.7 %; urban-mid (15,000–99,999) 15.4 %. Unemployment rate higher in larger localities: 3.6 % (≥100 mil) vs 1.7 % rural; urbano medio 2.9 %; urbano bajo 2.7 %. (p.4–p.5 Cuadro 2; p.12 Cuadro 6)
- **Observed (seasonally adjusted, q/q):** Unemployment 3.1 % (−0.1 pp); TIL1 −0.4 pp; TOSI1 −0.2 pp; suboccupation rate −0.1 pp. (p.10, p.11, p.14)
- **Observed (state dispersion, Q4 2022):** Highest participation BCS 69.2 %, Yucatán 66.3 %, Nayarit 65.7 %, Colima 65.4 %, Quintana Roo 65.2 %, Jalisco 62.7 %, Chihuahua and CDMX 62.6 %. Highest unemployment CDMX/Edomex 4.5 %, Tabasco 4.2 %. Highest informality Oaxaca 81.2 %, Guerrero 79.0 %, Chiapas 75.2 %. Lowest informal Coahuila 34.2 %, Nuevo León 35.8 %. Highest TCCO Chiapas 48.1 %; lowest Jalisco 15.1 %. (p.16–p.17; Cuadro 9)
- **Observed (39-city aggregate, Q4 2022):** Participation 61.6 %; unemployment 3.7 %; suboccupation 7.2 %; TCCO 26.2 %; TIL1 43.5 %. 64 % of occupied concentrated in 8 metro areas (CDMX, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Puebla, Tijuana, León, Ciudad Juárez, Mérida). (p.19; Cuadro 10)

## Methodology and limitations carried forward
- **Comparable series only via salario mínimo equivalente base enero 2022** for income-classified rates (TCCO; income-level counts in Cuadro 4 build from nominal salarios mínimos). INEGI publishes comparable series online. (p.9 footnote 1/; p.15; p.16 Gráfica 6 note; p.18 Cuadro 9 footnote 3/)
- **Pandemic classification change** (PNEA-disponible incl. ausentes temporales con vínculo + personas con necesidad o deseos de trabajar) operated Q3 2020 → Q2 2022; **discontinued** from Q3 2022 — structural break for some PNEA components relative to earlier quarters. (p.22–p.23; footnote * p.3)
- **Field mode:** phone+face-to-face mixed Q3 2020 → Q2 2022 (ENOEN); **face-to-face only** from Q3 2022 onward — another structural break. (p.21)
- **No sampling error, CVs, or confidence intervals reported in this note**; only point estimates with y/y and q/q differences. Footnote 5 (p.19) only validates metro-area inclusion for state-level comparability (interval-of-confidence comparison and 50-replica significance tests vs Q2/Q3 2019).
- **Document does not assert causality, intent, or competency attribution** to government policy; contains no policy-evaluation language.

## Skeptical/policy-critical angles supported by the text
- National averages mask deep regional gaps in informality (Oaxaca 81.2 % vs Coahuila 34.2 %) and TCCO (Chiapas 48.1 % vs Jalisco 15.1 %). (p.16–p.17; Cuadro 9)
- Aggregate unemployment and participation improved y/y, but **27 % of occupied still worked >48 h/week** and **6.2 % <15 h/week**; **22.6 % self-employed without employees** (cuenta propia sin personal pagado); **42.0 % of subordinate workers without written contract** (16.302 M / 39.775 M without contrato escrito vs 22.863 M con contrato escrito); **16.720 M without health-care access through work** (sin acceso a instituciones de salud). (Cuadros 3, 4)
- Tasa de Ocupación Parcial y Desocupación (TOPD1) 9.0 % — higher for women (12.6 %) than men (6.5 %). (p.15 Cuadro 8)
- Time-of-unemployment longer than 3 months fell to 15.2 % (≥3 months total rests across the 8.2 % + 5.0 % + 2.0 % sub-bands); duration of unemployment: >1 mo to ≤3 mo dropped 93 k; >3 mo to ≤6 mo −66,778; >6 mo to ≤1 yr −76 k; >1 yr −54,957 (≈−55 k). (p.13–p.14 Cuadro 7)

## Sections a stronger reviewer should reopen
- Verify whether the Q3-2022 PNEA reclassification affects the y/y comparison for PNEA-disponible (−2.071 M) and PNEA-no-disponible (+1.719 M) — partly mechanical. (p.3 Cuadro 1, footnote *)
- Verify survey-mode break (phone→face-to-face) impact on response rate and any nonresponse bias for Q4 2022 vs Q4 2021 (note is silent on response rates/CV).
- Confirm whether salario-mínimo-equivalente adjustments are already baked into reported TCCO or only available on INEGI's separate tabulados. (p.9 fn 1/; p.15; p.16 Gráfica 6 note)

## Caveats / traps honoured
- No inference of AMLO/government motive or causation. Headline figures are point estimates; sampling error not disclosed here.
- Quarter-to-quarter movements attributed by INEGI to seasonal adjustment, not to real economic regime change.
- All unit/percentage assertions reproduced verbatim from Cuadros 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 with page locators; no fabrication.

## VERIFIED ADDITIONS

1. **Sector breakdown counts (Q4 2022):** Primary 6.9 M (11.8 %); Secondary 14.5 M (24.9 %); Tertiary 36.6 M (62.7 %); remaining 0.6 % no especificó. (p.6)
   - Minimal paraphrase: Q4 2022 occupied population by sector — Primary 6.9 M (11.8 %); Secondary 14.5 M (24.9 %); Tertiary 36.6 M (62.7 %); 0.6 % not specified.
   - Locator: original extract p.6, ¶ "Por sector de actividad."
   - Note: matches the header labels reproduced in Cuadro 3, p.8.

2. **Long-duration unemployment sub-bands (Q4 2022):** >3 mo to ≤6 mo: 8.2 % (−1.7 pp y/y); >6 mo to ≤1 yr: 5.0 % (−2.7 pp); >1 yr: 2.0 % (−2.2 pp). (p.14 Cuadro 7)
   - Minimal paraphrase: Duration-of-unemployment sub-bands for Q4 2022 — 3–6 months 8.2 % (−1.7 pp); 6 months–1 year 5.0 % (−2.7 pp); >1 year 2.0 % (−2.2 pp).
   - Locator: original extract p.14, Cuadro 7 "Duración del desempleo" column.

3. **Subocupación sex split (Q4 2022):** Hombres 2.6 M (7.6 %); Mujeres 1.7 M (7.2 %). (p.10)
   - Minimal paraphrase: Subocupación by sex in Q4 2022 — men 2.6 M (7.6 % of occupied men); women 1.7 M (7.2 % of occupied women).
   - Locator: original extract p.10, ¶ "Población subocupada," second paragraph.

4. **State-level top participation (Q4 2022, full list):** BCS 69.2 %; Yucatán 66.3 %; Nayarit 65.7 %; Colima 65.4 %; Quintana Roo 65.2 %; Jalisco 62.7 %; Chihuahua and CDMX 62.6 % each. (p.16)
   - Minimal paraphrase: States with highest participation rate in Q4 2022 — BCS 69.2 %, Yucatán 66.3 %, Nayarit 65.7 %, Colima 65.4 %, Quintana Roo 65.2 %, Jalisco 62.7 %, Chihuahua 62.6 %, CDMX 62.6 %.
   - Locator: original extract p.16, ¶ "Las entidades federativas que presentaron las mayores tasas de participación…"

5. **TCCO low-end state list (Q4 2022):** Jalisco 15.1 %; Sinaloa 16.8 %; BCS 16.9 %; Nuevo León 16.9 %; Aguascalientes 19.4 %; Colima 20.7 %. (p.17)
   - Minimal paraphrase: States with lowest critical-occupation rates (TCCO) in Q4 2022 — Jalisco 15.1 %; Sinaloa 16.8 %; BCS 16.9 %; Nuevo León 16.9 %; Aguascalientes 19.4 %; Colima 20.7 %.
   - Locator: original extract p.17, final paragraph.

6. **Hours-worked distribution total split (Q4 2022):** <15 h 6.2 %; 15–34 h 17.0 %; 35–48 h 47.4 % (+1.4 pp y/y, +1.6 M); >48 h 27.0 % (−0.4 pp); ausentes temporales con vínculo laboral 1.4 %; no especificado 1.0 %. (p.6–p.7; p.8 Cuadro 3)
   - Minimal paraphrase: Hours-worked distribution of occupied population Q4 2022 — <15 h 6.2 %; 15–34 h 17.0 %; 35–48 h 47.4 % (+1.4 pp y/y); >48 h 27.0 %; ausentes temporales con vínculo laboral 1.4 %; no especificado 1.0 %.
   - Locator: original extract p.6–p.7 ¶ "Otras condiciones de trabajo"; p.8 Cuadro 3 "Duración de la jornada de trabajo."

7. **Unemployment sex counts (Q4 2022):** Hombres 1.050 M; Mujeres 746 k. (p.12)
   - Minimal paraphrase: Q4 2022 unemployed by sex — men 1.050 M; women 746 k.
   - Locator: original extract p.12, ¶ "En el trimestre de referencia, los hombres desocupados…"

## REOPEN REQUESTS

- The original extract (p.10) anchors suboccupation decline to "1.7 millones menos que en el mismo trimestre de 2021." The draft source map reproduced the headline "Suboccupation 4.4 M (7.5 %, −3.1 pp)" (Cuadro 8 implied) but does not separately retain the absolute y/y decrease. **Mapping note:** restored under VERIFIED ADDITIONS not applicable (the y/y decrease is implicit in the rate drop; the 7.5 % rate and the 4.4 M count are already in the source map's "national" line). Closing without further action.
- Microdata back-rebuilt to Q1 2014 (p.21 framing) — the source map carries this as a comparability flag but does not separately disclose whether any Cuadro 9/Cuadro 10 entity figure combines 2022 microdata with the prior population estimate. The note (p.21) only states "para la presente publicación se encuentran actualizados los microdatos y tabulados a partir del primer trimestre de 2014." No explicit scope statement is present in the extract.
- BCS unemployment top-tail call: the extract reports BCS state-level unemployment 2.9 % (Cuadro 9). The draft source map does not assert BCS as a top unemployment entity (it is not; CDMX/Edomex 4.5 % and Tabasco 4.2 % lead). No change required — closing.

*(Source map prepared per Ch.5B evidence-reader protocol; no scoring performed.)*
